key_assumptions.source: FY2025 cash generated from operating activities £308.0m ÷ 772.38m weighted average shares; capex ~£4m (low capital intensity per AR 2025)

open_questions: First onboard deep dive; download script and `registry.json` `ir_roots` should list `plc.rightmove.co.uk` for future refreshes.
Confirm live LSE price and whether FY2026 investment year should reduce starting free cash flow per share in base case.
Stance **accumulate** is model-driven (>20% IRR); portfolio default was **watch** at onboard.
thesis: Rightmove plc runs the dominant UK online property portal. **[Fact]** Estate agents and new-home developers pay subscription and product fees to advertise listings; home movers use the site for search, valuations, and research. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **£425.1 million**, up **9%**, with **underlying operating profit** of **£297.7 million** (70% margin). **[Fact]** The platform is asset-light: **£308.0 million** cash generated from operating activities on roughly **772 million** average shares. **[Fact]** Strategic growth areas (commercial property, mortgages, rental services) grew combined revenue **25%** year over year while the core agency membership base grew **1%**.
why_market_wrong: The market may be anchoring on **FY2026 guidance** for only **3–5%** underlying operating profit growth while the company accelerates AI and product investment. **[Inference]** That near-term margin pause can obscure a toll-booth model with **~89%** consumer time share on property portals (Comscore, cited in FY2025 results) and **ARPA** still rising (**6%** on core packages in FY2025). **[Inference]** At **443 pence** per share (LSE, 4 June 2026), owner cash yields roughly **9%** before growth, so the equity can look “fully priced” on earnings multiples yet still clear a mid-teens annual return on filing-based cash per share if buybacks and product mix persist.
